header: Date: 2028-12-05 | Time: 15:30 UTC | Duration: 52m | Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Lucas Patel (Redwood SE), Karen Ortiz (CISO - Northbridge), Dr. Evan Miles (Head of AI - Northbridge), Jordan Lee (IT Ops - Northbridge)
summary: POC scoping call focused on security/compliance requirements for a pilot: SOC2/ISO evidentiary materials, SSO/SAML integration (Okta), RBAC and audit log retention, encryption/KMS, data residency, and bench/size/timeline for success criteria. Agreed next steps: Redwood to provide security docs and run benchmark with customer-provided sample workloads; tentative bench run mid-December; pilot gating criteria enumerated.
topics: Security artifacts: SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001, penetration test summary
Authentication: SSO/SAML integration, Okta, SCIM, assertions
Authorization: RBAC granularity, admin vs dev vs auditor roles
Auditability: audit logs, retention, export, SIEM integration
Encryption & key management: at-rest, in-transit, KMS/HSM options
Deployment modes: hosted vs dedicated vs private (VPC/on-prem)
Benchmarks: success criteria, workload sizing, latency/throughput targets
Timeline & pilot gating: artifacts, approvals, bench run dates
transcript: 00:00 Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro — maya from Redwood AE, lucas our se. how are we on time?
00:08 Karen Ortiz: Good, thanks. we have about an hour blocked, big topic is security pilot requirements — SOC 2 and SSO mostly.
00:16 Lucas Patel: Great, we'll focus on scoping for the POC — success criteria, workload pics, benchmarks and timeline. i can cover technical bits.

00:25 Dr. Evan Miles: Quick background — we're standing up an assistant for clinician notes, will be running through protected health info, so compliance is huge. we have a security review team and need SOC2 + ISO artifacts and SSO integration for pilot users.
00:40 Jordan Lee: also network ops will need to know VPC peering and whether we need dedicated capacity or a private deployment for egress controls.

00:50 Lucas Patel: Understood. on Redwood side we offer three modes: hosted api, dedicated reserved pools, and private (VPC/on-prem). each has different isolation and audit capabilities. for HIPAA-like workflows customers often choose Dedicated or Private.

01:05 Maya Chen: from a commercial/pilot perspective we usually start hosted to move fast, then switch to dedicated if they need stricter controls. but we'll match your compliance needs — share docs soon.
01:15 Karen Ortiz: Can you confirm SOC 2 Type II coverage and ISO 27001? we need the report and scope — does it include the control environment around key management and logs?

01:28 Maya Chen: yes we have SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 attestations. we'll share the latest reports. scope includes our control plane and data handling; keys and HSM details are in the KMS appendix.
01:40 Dr. Evan Miles: How about SSO? Okta is our provider, we need SAML-based SSO and SCIM user provisioning for pilot users. also RBAC so auditors can't see sensitive prompts.

01:52 Lucas Patel: We support SAML and SCIM for provisioning and Okta is a common integration. RBAC can be configured per-account with admin/dev/auditor roles. we also have token-level auditing and per-route logs.
02:05 Jordan Lee: Audit logs — what's retention and how do we export to our SIEM? we need at least 1 year for pilot audit trail, preferably push to Splunk or S3 for retention.

02:17 Maya Chen: Audit logs are available via the console and can stream to your S3, or we can push to SIEM connectors. retention settings are configurable for Dedicated/Private; hosted has standard retention but we can discuss extended retention as an enterprise add-on.
02:32 Karen Ortiz: Encryption: at-rest and in-transit is expected but we need to know whether Redwood manages the keys or we can provision customer-managed keys (CMK/HSM).

02:44 Lucas Patel: We support customer-managed keys via KMS in Dedicated and Private modes; for hosted customers we offer KMS with Bring-Your-Own-Key options in some tiers. HSM-backed keys are an enterprise option.

02:58 Dr. Evan Miles: Benchmarking: we need to validate latency and quality. target for our use case is p95 latency under 400ms for 512-token responses and throughput to handle peak of ~200 concurrent sessions. also cost per 1k tokens needs to be estimated.

03:15 Lucas Patel: For benching we'll run a harness that simulates your workload distribution. can you confirm sequence lengths, average tokens per turn, and qps? helps us size batchers and model selection.

03:28 Dr. Evan Miles: Avg sequence ~220 tokens, some outliers to 800; expecting ~5k messages/day initially, burst to 200 concurrent in busiest hours. quality fallback is critical — we need stable outputs and rollback plan if model regression occurs.

03:45 Maya Chen: Success criteria suggestion: 1) security docs + SSO in place, 2) p95 latency < 400ms for 512 tokens on the test harness, 3) throughput to meet 200 concurrent with <10% error rate, 4) audit logs visible in your SIEM and retention confirmed. happy to adopt or modify.
04:05 Karen Ortiz: That aligns. also need a security review checklist: penetration test summary, data residency statement (all PHI must remain in us-east-1), and SLA for incident response.

04:18 Lucas Patel: We'll include pentest summaries and a data residency statement. regarding region pinning, Redwood can pin to AWS region for Dedicated/Private. hosted tier usually allows region selection but we'll clarify.
04:30 Jordan Lee: Network setup — do we need VPN or VPC peering? we'll prefer VPC peering to avoid internet egress for pilot traffic.

04:40 Lucas Patel: Private deployment supports VPC peering and direct connect; Dedicated can use private networking options; hosted uses TLS over the public internet unless you opt for a private link / peering add-on.
04:53 Dr. Evan Miles: Timeline — we'd like a 6-week pilot: week 0 discovery, week 1 bench, week 2 policy review, weeks 3-5 pilot run, week 6 review. is that realistic?
05:05 Maya Chen: Yes that's standard. immediate items: share docs this week, bench next week, pilot target start in two weeks. approvals often drive the final date though.
05:15 Karen Ortiz: Approvals: i'll need SOC2 doc and a one-pager on RBAC and logs for our security board. also a contact to validate scoping around PHI handling.
05:26 Maya Chen: We'll provide the SOC2/ISO docs and a tailored security FAQ. Lucas will be the technical lead for the bench and network details.

05:35 Lucas Patel: On the bench details — we'll run three workloads: 1) clinician note summarization (avg 220 tokens), 2) patient triage chat (short-turns, 80 tokens avg), 3) batch embedding job for indexing (large throughput). we'll measure p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec and cost per 1k tokens.
05:52 Dr. Evan Miles: For the embedding job, we need to see throughput for a 10M record index (can be done in batches); cost pro forma will matter for scale decisions.
06:05 Jordan Lee: can the bench be run in our VPC or do you need sample data only? we don't want PHI out during bench setup.

06:14 Lucas Patel: We can run the bench against a private deployment in your VPC or run a bench in our dedicated infra using sanitized/anonymized samples. for initial bench we prefer sanitized samples. for a full pilot we can set up VPC peering.

06:28 Maya Chen: We'll send a bench checklist with environment options. also note: for pilot gating we typically ask for a security sign-off after docs review and a bench run demonstrating the latency/throughput thresholds.
06:41 Karen Ortiz: On RBAC — auditors need read-only auditor role that can access logs but not prompt content. is that configurable?

06:50 Lucas Patel: Yes, roles are granular. you can restrict redwood console views and API keys so auditors get log access without seeing raw prompt text. we also support redaction/pseudonymization hooks before logs are stored.
07:03 Dr. Evan Miles: How reliable is fallback behavior? if model falls below quality thresholds, we need automatic rollback or toggle to a stable variant.

07:12 Lucas Patel: We support rollout policies including canary, A/B, and automatic fallback to pinned versions. Redwood Optimize can recommend quantization or smaller variants if you need cost/latency tuning.
07:24 Karen Ortiz: Any certifications around penetration testing and vulnerability disclosure? we need an internal contact for responsible disclosure.
07:33 Maya Chen: We'll include our vuln disclosure process and pentest summary. I'll add the security contact to the next email thread.
07:41 Jordan Lee: Regarding logs export — preferred format is JSONL over S3 with KMS encryption. can we get an example delivery method?

07:48 Lucas Patel: Yes we can push JSONL to S3 with envelope encryption using your CMK for Dedicated/Private; for hosted we'll provide encrypted streams with customer-managed key options if available in your tier.

08:00 Dr. Evan Miles: For success criteria, i'm capturing: security artifacts present; SSO working with Okta + SCIM; RBAC and auditor role validated; bench meets p95 and throughput; logs streaming to our SIEM and region pinning to us-east-1. anything else?
08:15 Maya Chen: That looks complete. we'll formalize the success criteria doc and share it. also we'll provide a schedule for the bench next week.
08:24 Karen Ortiz: One more — incident response SLA. we need a contact and escalation for security incidents during pilot, ideally 24/7 for severity 1.
08:34 Maya Chen: We'll include our incident response SLA and on-call contacts. enterprise tiers include tighter SLA windows.
08:42 Lucas Patel: ok will prep the bench plan and a short runbook for setting up a private peering test if you decide to go down that path.

08:52 Maya Chen: Next steps recap: i'll send SOC2/ISO + security FAQ; Lucas will send bench plan and test harness; Jordan will share sanitized samples and network contact; Karen will route internal approvers. we aim to run bench week of Dec 11-15.
09:10 Dr. Evan Miles: Sounds good. any objections or questions?
09:15 Karen Ortiz: no objections, just be mindful of PHI and logs — we will enforce pseudonymization during bench if needed.
09:22 Maya Chen: Understood. thanks everyone — we'll follow up by EOD with docs and calendar invites.
09:29 End of recording
